name: Insertion Sort
description: Builds a sorted portion one element at a time by inserting each new element into its correct position. Like sorting playing cards — pick up a card, slide it into the right spot.
aim: Sort by maintaining a growing sorted sub-array at the left. For each unsorted element, shift all greater sorted elements right and insert the element in its correct position.
howItWorks: Walk left through sorted portion, shifting elements greater than key rightward
Insert key where a smaller element is found or at index 0

time.bestCase: Array already sorted — zero shifts needed
time.worstCase: Reverse-sorted — maximum shifts for every element

complexity.spaceDescription: Single key variable for temporary storage

realWorld: Used in TimSort (Python/Java) for small sub-arrays
Online sorting — handles incoming stream one element at a time
Nearly sorted data appears frequently in real-world applications
whenToUse: Stable sort with O(1) extra space
Online algorithm — can sort as data arrives
alternatives: Shell Sort — improves by comparing distant elements first
Merge Sort — stable O(n log n) for larger datasets
Tim Sort — hybrid that uses insertion sort for small runs
